title: Register values during a decrement loop
statement: Let $P$ be a language of bit strings, let $x$ be a bit string, and let $B,i,u\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $i\le B$ and $u\le B$. For every $a,b\in\mathbb N$ with $b+2a\le B$, the program starts at its first decrement-loop label with register values $(i,a,b,u)$ and, after finitely many steps, reaches the next loop label with values $(i,0,b+2a,u)$ and no answer recorded. At every step before reaching that configuration, all four register values are at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a language of bit strings
